successors.name: Kingdom of Alamannia
successors.text: the Cliopatria row Kingdom of Alamannia, whose first shape is 462

ledger.x: 213: the Alemanni appear on the Roman frontier.
260: the Alemanni take the Agri Decumates.
about 300: the Agri Decumates are abandoned for good.
406: the Alemanni cross the Rhine and take Alsace.
461/462: the Alemanni become the Kingdom of Alamannia.

wars.name: Alemannic invasion of Italy and the evacuation of the Agri Decumates
wars.outcome: Gallienus defeated the Alemanni at Mediolanum in 259 ('300,000 Alemanni die'), yet the Romans evacuated the Agri Decumates and retreated behind the Rhine in 259-260, and the Alemanni captured them in 260.

wars.name: Alemannic invasion of Gaul and northern Italy
wars.outcome: Claudius II defeated the Alemanni at Lake Benacus in 268; Aurelian was defeated by the Alemanni invading Italy at Placentia in 271 and the Alemannic army was destroyed in 271.

wars.name: Probus's campaigns against the Alamanni
wars.outcome: Probus's 'successful campaigns against Goths, Alamanni, Longiones, Franks and Burgundians' (Germanic Wars page); the Agri Decumates page: Probus 'definitely recaptured the area'.

wars.name: Julian's campaigns against the Alemanni (Battle of Strasbourg)
wars.outcome: Roman double victory under Constantius II in 354-355; Siege of Autun 356; 'Roman invasion of Alemannic territory led by general Barbatio and Julian' in 357 and Julian 'expels the Alemanni from the Rhineland' at Strasbourg (357); several Alemannic kings 'in…

wars.name: Valentinian I's campaigns against the Alemanni
wars.outcome: The Alemanni crossed the frozen Rhine on 2 January 366 after the invasion of Gaul in 365 and the sack of Moguntiacum in 367; Valentinian invaded 'Alemannic territory' in 368 (Solicinium) and Macrian was 'deposed in an expedition ordered by Valentinian I in…

wars.name: Alemannic invasion of Italy (Campi Cannini)
wars.outcome: 'Alemanni invade Italy and are defeated near Lake Maggiore by Majorian' (457).

certainty.note: No page draws the Alemannic frontier; the Agri Decumates follow the Roman limes line (Rheinbrohl to Pforring) only from the Roman side.
